canvas-01-1.description: The left half of printed sheet 1, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, shows Washington Avenue where it crosses the Raritan River Railroad on the north-east side of Milltown. The railroad runs straight up the sheet with several parallel tracks and sidings; beside it stand the passenger station, a freight house and a long coal platform. North of Washington Avenue is the yard of Kuhlthau Bros. Co., dealers in coal, hay and feed, with wagon sheds, hay and feed warehouses and a fertilizer house. South of the avenue, sidings curve off the main line towards the works of the Royston Paper Co., makers of fancy papers (coloring only), whose manufacturing building, stock room and office stand in an otherwise open lot. A few dwellings and a store are drawn at the west edge, where the sheet adjoins sheet 2. Much of the half is open ground. The right half of the sheet holds the title, a key map of the whole town, the street and specials index and an inset of the Milltown Mfg. Co. works on Riders Lane; those are not part of this map part. A large compass rose sits in the open ground south of Washington Avenue, and a 50-foot scale bar runs along the bottom.
notes: Placed from a single control point, the crossing of Washington Avenue with the railroad (today the Sayreville Running Track), with the scale set to 8.0 px/ft and the rotation taken from the measured lines: low confidence.
The Raritan River Railroad is today the Sayreville Running Track in OpenStreetMap.

Printed sheet 1. Left: Washington Av at the Raritan River R.R. passenger station, Kuhlthau Bros coal yard, Royston Paper Co. (50 ft). Right: title, key map of the town (not to scale, masked out), index, and bottom inset of the Milltown Mfg Co. works on Riders Lane. Two map parts.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Milltown Mfg Co. (leather stains and stuffings) on Riders Lane (no street junction; only Riders Lane drawn, the Raritan River R.R. crossing (Ryders Lane / Sayreville Running Track) is at or beyond the inset's lower edge; needs hand-picked control: Ryders Lane rail crossing plus px_per_ft and north_deg, or parcel corners on Ryders Lane).

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch, covers Main Street from the Lawrence Brook bridge south to Sand Street, at the western edge of the borough beside Mill Pond. At the top, Main Street crosses Lawrence Brook on a steel bridge, and a spur of the Raritan River Railroad crosses the brook on an iron bridge to reach the Public Service Corporation of New Jersey car barn, a large brick trolley barn with a car repair shop and former power and boiler houses, standing in the angle of Main Street and Washington Avenue. North-east along Washington Avenue are the brick buildings of the Russel Playing Card Co. (Michelin Tire Co. owner of buildings), with a reservoir and a siding to the railroad. South of Washington Avenue, Main Street is lined with frame dwellings and stores, the Hotel Marguerite, the parsonage and St. Paul's Reformed Church with a building to be its Sunday school. Water Street runs west from Main Street towards Mill Pond, and a brook crosses the open land east of Main Street diagonally. At the bottom, along Sand Street, stands the Borough Water Works pumping station with a covered reservoir. Much of the eastern half of the sheet is open lots. The north arrow and a 50-foot scale bar are drawn on the left side and bottom.
notes: Main Street south of Washington Avenue is today South Main Street.
Sand Street appears to be today's West Lakewood Avenue (its junctions with Main and 1st Streets match).
Placed from two junctions on Main Street (helmert): low confidence.
Main St from Lawrence Brook bridge and Washington Av (Public Service car barn, Russel Playing Card Co.) south to Sand St. 50 ft to an inch. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: The left part of sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers Main Street from Sand Street south to William Street in the southern part of Milltown. At the top, Sand Street runs west to Water Street and Lawrence Brook, crossed by 1st Street; the borough hall and fire engine house stand on Main Street a little to the south. Kuhlthau Avenue runs diagonally south-west from Main Street, lined with small frame dwellings. Further south, Handy, Henry and William Streets run east from Main Street to Christopher Street, and George Street and Lincoln Avenue form a small grid of lots west of Main Street. The district is residential: frame dwellings and outbuildings, a few stores, and large open lots. Below William Street Main Street continues south past a street marked not open, and a note at the bottom records a group of five frame dwellings about 300 feet further on. A heavy line separates this part from the two parts on the right of the sheet. North arrow and scale bar are drawn on the sheet.
notes: Main Street is today South Main Street; Lincoln Avenue is East and West Lincoln Avenue.
Sand Street appears to be today's West Lakewood Avenue.
Christopher Street and Handy Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
Main Street junctions with Sand Street and Kuhlthau Avenue were hand-picked; the fit is poor (RMSE about 4.5 m): low confidence.

Three parts, all 100 ft: part 1 Main St from Sand St to William St (Kuhlthau Av, Lincoln Av); part 2 top right Philadelphia & Boston Brick Co. (closed) and Marcus Wright clay shipping on the Raritan River R.R., no street; part 3 Riva Av, Lafayette Av, Scott Av, Sherman Av to Church St (Michelin Tire Co. houses).

Not georeferenced on this sheet: Philadelphia & Boston Brick Co. (closed) and Marcus Wright clay shipping on the Raritan River R.R. (no street; only railroad sidings drawn; needs step 6b: a rail feature matched to the modern Sayreville Running Track, or parcel corners).

sheet-3-3.description: The lower right part of sheet 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows the Michelin Tire Co. housing development in the south-west of Milltown, between Riva Avenue and Church Street. Riva Avenue and Lafayette Avenue run diagonally across the part, lined with rows of identical frame dwellings on narrow lots; Scott Avenue and Sherman Avenue run south from Lafayette Avenue to Church Street, with further rows of dwellings. Below Church Street are Michelin Tire Co. bunk houses. Parsons Lane crosses the open ground at the top, and Broad Street enters at the right edge. The rest of the part is open land. The part is separated by heavy lines from the main part of the sheet on the left and the brick works above.
notes: Lafayette Avenue is today Lafayette Street; Church Street is West Church Street.
Parsons Lane is not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the centre of Milltown: Main Street from Riva Avenue south to Ford Avenue, and the grid of residential streets west of it to Sherman Avenue. Riva, Richter, Cottage and Broad Streets, Church Street and Ford Avenue cross the sheet; South and Clay Streets run parallel to Main Street. East of Main Street are John Street, Elm Place, School Street and Vanderbilt Avenue. Most blocks are filled with frame dwellings. Main Street carries the business buildings: the fire department hose company and borough hall, the post office, a bank, stores, and the Milltown Public School; east of Main Street are the Milltown M.E. Church, the Community House (picture shows), the French school and club, and a sewage disposal and electric light plant. The Michelin Athletic Association grounds with bleachers occupy the west side. Along the bottom of the sheet the long brick buildings of the Michelin Tire Co. works line the shore of Mill Pond, marked mutual risk, admittance refused; Main Street crosses Lawrence Brook on a bridge at the lower right.
notes: Main Street is today North Main Street; Church Street is West Church Street; Lafayette Avenue is Lafayette Street; Cottage is Cottage Avenue; La Fayette Avenue is Lafayette Street.
The Michelin Tire Co. works fill the south edge along Mill Pond.
Town centre: Main St from Riva Av to Ford Av, South St to Elm Pl, Michelin Tire Co. works along Mill Pond. 100 ft. One part. Pilot sheet.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the northern part of Milltown east of Main Street, from Riva and Vanderbilt Avenues north to Lawrence Avenue. Main Street runs up the left side, crossed by a trolley right-of-way; east of it Herbert, Harrison and Cleveland Avenues, Booream Avenue, Van Liew Avenue and Vanderbilt Avenue run across the sheet, with Willow Street, Chestnut Street and Lawrence Avenue running north-south. Yarnell Avenue and Lawrence Avenue branch off at the top, with Garver Avenue, Columbia Avenue, Fulton Street and Cortlandt Street at the upper right. The district is a new suburb: most lots are laid out but empty, with scattered frame dwellings, concentrated along Booream and Van Liew Avenues and along Main Street. The R.C. Church of Our Lady of Lourdes stands on Main Street, and a concrete block works on Lawrence Avenue. Large open blocks lie on both sides.
notes: Main Street junctions were left out: they carried residuals of 6 to 7 m (the modern North Main Street centre is off its 1924 line here).
Lawrence Avenue is today East Lawrence Street.
North Main St from Riva/Vanderbilt to Lawrence Av, Herbert, Harrison, Cleveland, Booream, Van Liew; Lawrence Av, Willow, Chestnut. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, covers the north end of Milltown around Main Street north of Lawrence Avenue. Main Street runs up the middle; west of it Prospect Avenue, Stelle Avenue, Lewis Avenue, Tremont Avenue and Lawrence Avenue form a grid of large, mostly empty lots, and east of it Elkins Avenue, Fulton Street, Cortlandt Street, Garver Avenue and Columbia Avenue run north-east and south-east from Main Street. Buildings are few: scattered frame dwellings along Main Street, Lewis Avenue and Stelle Avenue, and a standpipe on Elkins Avenue. Much of the part is laid-out but unbuilt subdivision. Heavy lines separate it from the two insets at the top of the sheet.
notes: Tremont Avenue is today Tremont Street; Lawrence Avenue is East and West Lawrence Street; Elkins Avenue is Elkins Lane.
Lewis Avenue and Fulton Street are not in OpenStreetMap.
Garver Avenue junctions were rejected (13 to 15 m off).

Three parts, all 100 ft: part 1 Main St north of Lawrence Av (Prospect, Lewis, Tremont, Stelle, Elkins, Cortlandt, Garver, Columbia); part 2 top-left inset Main St at Haig, Foch and Pershing Avs (south end of town); part 3 top-right Booream and Van Liew Avs east of sheet 5 with Milltown Coal & Lumber Co.

sheet-6-2.description: The top-left inset of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, shows Main Street at the south end of Milltown, crossed by Haig, Foch and Pershing Avenues and with Vaun Street (arbitrary) at the bottom. Rows of nearly identical frame dwellings line both sides of Foch and Pershing Avenues and Main Street; Haig Avenue at the top has a shorter row. East of Main Street the land is vacant. The inset is turned to its own north arrow and separated from the rest of the sheet by heavy lines.
notes: This inset lies at the south end of town, about 1.2 km from the main part of the sheet.
Main Street here is today South Main Street; Foch Avenue is East and West Foch Avenue.
Placed from three junctions along Main Street (helmert): low confidence.

Three parts, all 100 ft: part 1 Main St north of Lawrence Av (Prospect, Lewis, Tremont, Stelle, Elkins, Cortlandt, Garver, Columbia); part 2 top-left inset Main St at Haig, Foch and Pershing Avs (south end of town); part 3 top-right Booream and Van Liew Avs east of sheet 5 with Milltown Coal & Lumber Co.

sheet-6-3.description: The top-right inset of sheet 6, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, continues sheet 5 east along Booream Avenue and Van Liew Avenue to the borough line. Narrow lots line both avenues, mostly empty, with a few frame dwellings. On the south side of Van Liew Avenue is the yard of the Milltown Coal & Lumber Co., with a planing mill, lumber sheds, a coal shed and lumber piles served by a railroad siding. The borough line is marked at the right edge.
notes: No street junction is drawn: placed from one point carried from sheet 5 (a building in block 36) with the scale and rotation set in the config: low confidence.

Three parts, all 100 ft: part 1 Main St north of Lawrence Av (Prospect, Lewis, Tremont, Stelle, Elkins, Cortlandt, Garver, Columbia); part 2 top-left inset Main St at Haig, Foch and Pershing Avs (south end of town); part 3 top-right Booream and Van Liew Avs east of sheet 5 with Milltown Coal & Lumber Co.
